parameters.content:
## Document Lifecycle Sync — added on top of the original ingestion workflow

Original manual batch flow (Run KB Ingestion -> ... -> Pinecone Insert) is UNCHANGED in shape, just extended with entry-point-agnostic config passing so it can be shared by 3 new triggers.

### New entry points
- 'New File Added' (Drive Trigger, fileCreated) -> reuses Download File -> Switch -> Prep Metadata -> ... -> Pinecone Insert -> registers in Indexed_Documents.
- 'File Updated' (Drive Trigger, fileUpdated) -> deletes old vectors for that file_id FIRST, then reprocesses through the SAME shared chain (no duplicate vectors).
- 'Check For Deleted Files' (hourly schedule) -> lists current Drive files, diffs against the Indexed_Documents registry, deletes Pinecone vectors for any file no longer present, marks the registry row Deleted. Drive has no native delete trigger, so this poll+diff is the simplest reliable alternative (see main answer for why the Changes API / push notifications were NOT used).

### Required manual setup (see full summary in chat)
1. Fill `pinecone_host` and `registry_sheet_id` in 'Ingestion Config' AND in the 3 new 'Attach Clinic Config (...)' Set nodes (values must match).
2. Create an HTTP Header Auth credential named 'Pinecone Data API (Header Auth)' — header name `Api-Key`, value = your Pinecone API key.
3. Create a Google Sheet with 2 tabs: `Indexed_Documents` and `Ingestion_Errors` (columns in chat summary).
4. Re-select the Google Sheets / Google Drive credentials on the new nodes.

nodes.name: Why deletion is a query-then-delete-by-id pair

parameters.content: n8n's Pinecone LangChain node has no delete-by-metadata operation (insert/load only), so this uses Pinecone's REST API directly via HTTP Request nodes. IMPORTANT: Pinecone SERVERLESS indexes do NOT support deleting by a metadata filter directly — only pod-based indexes do. To work on both, each deletion point first calls POST {host}/query with the google_drive_file_id filter (using a dummy zero-vector, since /query requires one) to collect the matching vector IDs, then calls POST {host}/vectors/delete with those explicit ids. `pinecone_host` (from the Pinecone console's Index page) and `embedding_dimension` (1536 for text-embedding-3-small, matching Embeddings OpenAI (KB)) are one-time config values rather than looked up dynamically, to keep this simple.
